issues.legal_issue: A grant of testamentary administration does not prevent a land lessor from investigating whether a bequest of leasehold property is a sale disguised as a will.
material_facts: The deceased allottee executed a will in favour of a person who was not related to him by blood.
Letters of Administration were granted on the basis of the will.
The land authority was not given notice of the testamentary proceedings.
The authority alleged that the will was actuated by monetary consideration and was in substance a sale contrary to its policy.
issues.conclusion: The grant of Letters of Administration did not preclude the authority from investigating the true nature of the transaction.
issues.legal_principle: A testamentary court determines whether the testator executed the instrument of his free will; a grant of probate or Letters of Administration does not confer title and merely enables administration of the estate. Title may still be disputed. Under section 6 of the Delhi Development Act, 1975, the authority may manage and dispose of land subject to applicable law. Its policies and guidelines bind the parties in the absence of rules to the contrary, and the authority may investigate whether a purported will is a sale in disguise, particularly when it had no notice of the testamentary proceedings.

predicates.leasehold_property_allocated_by_public_a: A public authority allocated property to a person under leasehold terms.
predicates.will_transfers_property_to_nonrelative: The allottee's will purports to transfer the property to a person who is not the allottee's relative.
predicates.testamentary_administration_granted: A court granted probate or Letters of Administration in relation to the will.
predicates.authority_not_notified_of_testamentary_p: The public authority was not notified of the proceeding in which testamentary administration was granted.

issues.definition: When leasehold property allocated by a public authority is purportedly transferred by will to a nonrelative and testamentary administration is granted without notice to the authority, the authority may investigate the true nature of the transfer.

issues.legal_issue: A lessor may enforce lease conditions requiring consent and payment of a share of unearned increase when a transfer or devolution of leasehold property breaches those conditions.
material_facts: The lease deed restricted sale, transfer, assignment, or parting with possession without the lessor's prior written consent and provided for recovery of fifty per cent of unearned increase when consent was given.
The lease deed also addressed involuntary transfers and required notice and supporting documents when title was transferred or devolved.

The authority had adopted guidelines addressing transfers under wills to persons outside the allottee's family, including where a purported will might conceal a transfer during the allottee's lifetime.
The respondent sought mutation on the basis of a will in her favour, was not related to the deceased allottee, and had not complied with the lease conditions.
The parties agreed on the amount payable as unearned increase, and the Court directed that possession not be delivered until payment.
issues.conclusion: The authority was entitled to invoke the lease conditions and demand unearned increase; the High Court's contrary judgment was set aside. The agreed amount was to be paid before possession was delivered.
issues.legal_principle: Clauses 4, 5, and 8 of the lease deed restricted transfers, provided for recovery of fifty per cent of unearned increase in the circumstances specified, and required notice of transfers or devolution. The authority's applicable policy guidelines could also be enforced in the absence of rules to the contrary. The authority was therefore competent to invoke the lease conditions where the transferee had not complied with them.

predicates.leasehold_property_subject_to_transfer_c: The property was held under a lease that restricted transfers and provided for recovery of unearned increase.
predicates.transfer_or_devolution_of_title: Title to the leased property was transferred or devolved to another person.
predicates.transferee_failed_to_comply_with_lease_c: The person receiving title did not comply with applicable consent, notice, or document requirements in the lease.
predicates.authority_policy_covers_such_transfer: The authority had a policy addressing the kind of transfer or devolution at issue.

issues.definition: If title to property subject to transfer conditions is transferred or devolves, the recipient fails to comply with the lease conditions, and the authority's policy covers the transfer, the lessor may recover unearned increase before delivering possession.

issues.legal_issue: A consumer claimant is not entitled to a refund of unearned increase when the underlying demand for that payment is upheld.
material_facts: The respondent in the consumer appeal had paid the unearned increase demanded by the authority.
After a judgment against the authority, the respondent sought and obtained a refund through the consumer fora.
The Court set aside the judgment that had undermined the authority's demand.
issues.conclusion: The respondent was not entitled to a refund, and the authority's appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Once the judgment on which the refund depended was set aside and the underlying demand for unearned increase was upheld, the respondent had no entitlement to recover the payment.

predicates.consumer_refund_proceeding: A consumer proceeding sought repayment of a sum paid to a public authority.
predicates.unearned_increase_paid: The claimant had paid the authority an amount demanded as unearned increase.
predicates.underlying_demand_for_payment_upheld: The court upheld the authority's entitlement to demand the payment.

issues.definition: In a consumer proceeding, when the claimant paid unearned increase and the underlying demand is upheld, the refund claim must be rejected.
